const p=load("page").text;
const oldStatus=p.slice(p.indexOf("## Implementation status"),p.indexOf("## Scope:"));
const current=`## Current product — Conversation Coach
Updated <mention-date start="2026-10-10"/> from the local working tree, including uncommitted work.
**Pitch:** Practise a difficult conversation, understand what worked, then rehearse a better answer. A playful sunflower makes practice approachable; evidence-backed reports and repeat sessions make it useful.
### What we have now
- **Rehearsal studio:** animated sunflower, scenario outfits in a wardrobe, Aura visualizer, focus/full-stage controls, and friendly, neutral or challenging counterparts.
- **Eight scenarios:** job interview, asking for a raise, relationship breakup, difficult feedback, flatmate conversation, cold call, bazaar negotiation and a custom situation.
- **Three ways to answer:** hands-free live voice with automatic turn taking and interruptions; manually recorded answers; typed messages. Both voice modes show an accumulating live transcript.
- **Adaptive responses:** short in-character replies using conversation history. Wording-based tone detection changes expression and automatic voice choice; Marshall and Lainey are optional voice overrides.
- **Detailed coaching:** strengths, improvements, suggested phrasing and scored dimensions with quoted evidence. Interview coaching adds target-role context, answer-by-answer reviews, a heatmap, one priority, a drill and the next session’s goal. “Practise this answer” starts a focused retry.
- **Local profile and growth:** saved transcripts/reports, comparable-session trends, skill filters, recurring strengths and improvement themes linked to supporting reports, and a practice-completion tracker. Completing a drill records practice, not proof of improved performance.
- **Recorded voice review:** microphone audio saved locally, separate verbatim transcription, hesitation counts, clickable timestamps, playback and frequency comparisons. Failed analysis can be retried while recordings remain playable.
### What changed from the original plan
The push-to-talk prototype has grown into a **practise → review → retry → track progress** loop. We now have a distinctive sunflower/wardrobe experience, continuous voice, richer coaching and local history. Recorded audio is now retained for review; the original “no raw recordings” assumption is superseded.
### Current technical shape
- Next.js, React and TypeScript; server routes keep provider keys out of browser code.
- Gradium streaming STT → Gemini text reply → Gradium streamed TTS. Manual recording also has a final WAV transcription path.
- Configured defaults in source: \`gemini-3.5-flash-lite\` for conversation, \`gemini-3.1-pro-preview\` for reports, and \`gemini-3.5-transcribe\` for recorded-audio review. Environment overrides can change these.
- Reports live in the browser-local profile; WAV recordings live in IndexedDB. Latest 50 sessions retained, with linked audio removed on deletion/eviction. No accounts or cross-device sync.
- Recording is capped at 10 minutes per session, split into clips of at most 60 seconds. Audio is sent to providers for processing; local storage does not mean offline processing.
### Verified now / still open
**Fresh checks for this update:** 273 unit/API tests pass; TypeScript check passes. This supersedes the earlier 178-pass/17-fail audit. These tests use mocked providers.
**Previously recorded evidence in README:** dedicated audio browser tests and synthetic live-provider checks passed. Those were not rerun for this documentation update; a full current browser suite and physical-microphone rehearsal are not newly verified.
- [ ] Run one complete demo on the actual microphone/headset: start, interrupt, finish, review, replay and restart. Check echo and latency.
- [ ] Run the full browser suite against the final integrated checkout; an earlier README run recorded a timing-sensitive live-transcript failure that passed in isolation.
- [ ] Before a public live-voice demo, protect voice-token issuance. It currently accepts localhost only.
**Interpretation limits:** tone comes from wording, not acoustic emotion detection. Scores, filler detection and timing are coaching estimates. Recurring themes need evidence from at least two comparable reports. Live feedback collection during conversation is not wired up; only its validated storage connector exists.
### Ideas / possible next steps
These are proposals, not implemented features or agreed commitments.
- **Immediate demo focus:** show one clear improvement loop, rather than touring every chart. Interview practice demonstrates the deepest coaching; bazaar negotiation is a quick playful opener.
- **Live coaching cues:** connect the existing live-feedback connector to lightweight hints at appropriate moments, while keeping the counterpart in character.
- **Personalised practice:** use recurring evidence to suggest the next scenario or drill and revisit the same question after practice.
- **Recruitment direction from the original brainstorm:** voice-led profile discovery, identify what matters to the person, then filter and match jobs. This would be a separate expansion beyond conversation rehearsal.
- **Broader personal dashboard from the original brainstorm:** voice-led goals, habits and plans. Keep this as a future direction until the core coaching loop is proven.
**Demo outline:** <mention-page url="https://app.notion.com/p/3f5d67cd0a0580429621ce39f628619a"/>
---
`;

**“Practise the conversations that matter before having them for real.”**
Proposed walkthrough, based on the current local implementation. Updated <mention-date start="2026-10-10"/>.
### Main demo: practise → review → retry
1. **Choose the situation.** Open the sunflower wardrobe, select Job interview, set the difficulty and target role.
2. **Have a short conversation.** Start live voice and give two or three answers. Show the live transcript, spoken replies and sunflower states. Briefly demonstrate interruption if the microphone setup has been rehearsed.
3. **End and learn.** Open the coaching report. Expand one answer to show the original words, quoted evidence and one concrete improvement.
4. **Listen back.** Once audio analysis finishes, play the recording and click a detected hesitation timestamp, if present. Explain that these are estimates, not a perfect count of every filler.
5. **Try again.** Select “Practise this answer” and use the suggested improvement.
6. **Show progress.** Open My profile. With genuine comparable prior sessions, show trends and recurring themes. A first session will not have comparison evidence.
### Features worth highlighting
- A recognisable sunflower character with outfits tied to scenarios.
- Natural voice conversation using Gradium STT and streamed TTS.
- Separate fast conversation and richer coaching model paths.
- Feedback grounded in the user’s actual answers.
- Local saved reports, audio replay and targeted practice.
**Optional opener:** Bazaar negotiation for a short, playful exchange before showing the interview coaching depth.
### Before presenting
- [ ] Rehearse on the actual laptop and headset, including interruption, audio review and restart.
- [ ] Prepare genuine prior sessions at matching scenario/difficulty/role if showing progress.
- [ ] Check provider access and report/audio-analysis latency; analysis runs after coaching and may take longer.
- [ ] Use localhost for continuous voice unless protected public token issuance has been implemented.
- [ ] Keep typed input available if microphone capture fails; it demonstrates conversation and coaching but cannot demonstrate audio analysis.
### Claims to keep accurate
Fresh unit/API check: **273 tests pass**, and typecheck passes. This is not proof of a physical-microphone demo.
Profiles and recordings are local to this browser; processing still uses external providers. There are no accounts or cross-device sync. Tone adaptation is based on words; live in-conversation coaching cues remain a future idea.
